title: sdk-rapid-starter-lab-notebook-draft
content:
Purpose
This note is a compact, pragmatic lab notebook for running a 25-minute SDK starter session for engineers evaluating Redwood’s client libraries. The goal is to get a reproducible light-weight loop (local dev -> sample request -> telemetry) that surfaces common friction points and creates a short checklist we can embed in larger onboarding flows.

Audience
- New SDK adopters: product engineers, full-stack devs, platform engineers who need a tiny repro.
- DX engineers building labs and smoke-tests.

Constraints & design decisions
- Keep infra zero-config: use the hosted Redwood sandbox API key and a local stub server if network is blocked.
- No heavy deps: favor curl, node (or python) with single-file examples, and a minimal docker (optional).
- Focus on first-success: one successful chat/generation call + basic latency and cost telemetry.

Prerequisites (assume 10 minutes prep)
1) Sign up / have sandbox API key: REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY (we provide short-lived demo keys during workshops).
2) Local machine: node 18+ or python 3.11+. curl installed.
3) Terminal + editor.
4) Optional: Docker for the local-proxy path.

Session outline (25 minutes)
- 0:00–02:00 Quick brief (intent, expected outcome)
- 02:00–08:00 Environment setup (export key, install sample)
- 08:00–16:00 Make your first call (sync then stream), examine response
- 16:00–20:00 Turn on lightweight telemetry: measure latency & tokens
- 20:00–23:00 Failure modes + local stub path
- 23:00–25:00 Next steps & follow-ups (docs, PR template)

Quick commands (Node)
1) Install minimal client (one-liner):
   npm install @redwood/sdk-lite --save && node -e "console.log('installed')"
2) One-file example (index.js) — pseudo-code:
   const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk-lite');
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY });
   async function main(){
     const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-mini-1', prompt: 'Write a 2-line haiku about latency' });
     console.log(r.text);
   }
   main().catch(e=>console.error(e));
3) Run: REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY=sk-demo node index.js

Quick commands (curl)
- POST example (sync):
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-mini-1","prompt":"Summarize this repo in two sentences"}' | jq .

Streaming (demo fallback)
- Show streaming using the client library or curl with SSE. If environment blocks SSE, show the polling fallback: request with streaming=false and poll status endpoint.

Telemetry: what to capture in the lab
- Wall latency (ms) for first token and full response
- Input token count and output token count (approx)
- Model name and a small quality flag (pass/fail) based on a single sample prompt
- Error class if any (auth, rate limit, model-unavailable)

Minimal telemetry snippet (node)
   const start = Date.now();
   const r = await client.generate(...);
   const latency = Date.now() - start;
   console.log(`latency_ms:${latency}`);
   console.log(`tokens_in:${r.tokens.in} tokens_out:${r.tokens.out}`);

Failure modes & quick mitigations (for workshop helpers)
- 401 Unauthorized: check env var, show how to print key and mask it in logs.
- 429 Rate limit: demonstrate using a small backoff (exponential with jitter).
- 503 Model busy: show model-fallback header and how to route to a cheaper/compatible model.
- Streaming broken in corp networks: fall back to polling sync endpoint or use a local stub.

Local stub path (5 minutes)
- Purpose: allow hands-on in air-gapped rooms or flaky Wi‑Fi.
- Approach: provide a single-file node server that mimics generate endpoint and returns canned responses + token accounting.
- Command: node local-stub.js (listens on 127.0.0.1:8080) and export REDWOOD_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080
- Keep stub simple: echo prompt + add small deterministic latency.

Checklist for finalizing the lab (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Create a one-file local-stub.js checked into sdk-examples repo (PR referenced above).
- [ ] Capture rare network failure repros and add to trouble-shooting appendix.
- [ ] Add a Prometheus-friendly telemetry exporter sample (pushgateway or local file).
- [ ] Make a 3-slide deck for workshop leads with cues and expected time per step.

Quick README template (for embedding in repos)
Title: Redwood SDK Rapid Starter Lab
Purpose: One-page, one-file demo to get a generation call and basic telemetry.
Requirements: node 18+, curl, REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY
Run: REDWOOD_SANDBOX_KEY=sk-demo node index.js
Notes: If network blocked, run node local-stub.js and set REDWOOD_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080

Troubleshooting notes for helpers
- "Nothing prints" → check console.error output and increase client log level: set REDWOOD_SDK_LOG=debug
- "We got an empty text" → inspect r.choices[0] vs r.error; show how to print r.raw for debugging
- "High cost" → run the same prompt with max_tokens=32 and compare token counts, show how to enable caching in client (prefix cache).

Retention & follow-ups
- Capture the telemetry CSV after each workshop and drop into the shared folder /training/sdklabs/attendance-telemetry/ for later analysis.
- Run a 1-week follow-up survey (3 questions: first success, biggest blocker, interest in more labs) and attach results to the Jira ticket.

Open questions (still need decisions)
- Do we ship demo API keys from console or use ephemeral token service? (security wants ephemeral).
- Standardize a telemetry schema for labs (field names, units) so we can automatically ingest results.
- Is there appetite for a browser-based 5-minute demo (would need CORS policy + simplified SDK bundle).

Notes to self (fragmented)
- Consider a "safety card" quick note: how to redact PII in examples.
- Add a tiny checklist for enterprise demos that require dedicated account mapping.
- Liaise with SRE to make a cheap, low-cost model variant specifically for workshops (reduce token spend).

Appendix: local stub pseudo-code hints
- express server with POST /v1/generate; compute token heuristic by splitting on whitespace; return a JSON shaped like our API with tokens.{in,out} and a text field: `Echo: ${prompt.slice(0,120)}`; sleep for 120ms to simulate small latency.

End.
